article_sentences: A Public Interest Litigation filed in the Supreme Court on September 25, 2026, by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi has brought an unprecedented internal rift within the Election Commission of India into the judicial spotlight.

It seeks the initiation of criminal proceedings against the Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, as well as a probe into the alleged unilateral orders of the CEC by forming a Special Investigation Team.

As per Indian Express expose, fourteen formal written objections to the Chief Election Commissioner's executive orders by the Election Commissioners Dr. Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Dr. Vivek Joshi were documented over a period of ten months, which cannot be dismissed as routine administrative friction.

The internal breach regarding the Chief Election Commissioner's unilateral executive orders without collective decision-making, the modification of voter registration rules via updates to digital portals, and the centralization of electoral rolls management in Delhi represent direct violations of multi-member decision-making obligations per the Representation of the People Act, 1950 and the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.

The Election Commission's official defense, issued on September 23, 2026, and reiterated following an all-member meeting on September 26, 2026, that written notes merely reflect standard internal deliberation fails statutory scrutiny.
In T.N. Seshan.

Union of India, the Supreme Court unambiguously denied the possibility of the existence of a supreme Chief Election Commissioner, as the statutory scheme was purposefully devised to prevent arbitrary executive governance.
The violation of this results in transforming the internal dispute into administrative illegality.
Multi-Member Governance or Monocratic Rule?
The statutory framework governing the internal decision-making process is established in Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023.
Per Section 18(2), the Commission shall transact its business unanimously.
Where there is a difference of opinion between the Chief Election Commissioner and the other Election Commissioners, then the matter will be decided according to the opinion of the majority.

article_sentences: Congress workers staged a protest rally in Hubballi on October 11, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of electoral malpractice and attempts to undermine democracy.

The rally was organised by the Vidyanagar and Unkal block Congress committees under the leadership of Rajat Ullagaddimath, Chairperson of the Hubballi-Dharwad City District Guarantee Schemes Implementation Authority.
It began at Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Circle, where the protesters read out Article 326 of the Constitution, which provides for elections based on adult suffrage.
Addressing the gathering, Mr. Ullagaddimath alleged that the RSS is conspiring to deprive oppressed and marginalised communities of their right to vote.
Describing the struggle to protect democracy and the Constitution as a ‘second freedom struggle’ against what he termed fascist forces, he called for concerted action to safeguard electoral rights.

Hundreds of Congress workers accused the BJP-led Union Government of attempting to manipulate the votes of Other Backward Classes, Economically Weaker Sections, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and minority communities.
They raised slogans against the Centre and demanded Mr. Kumar’s resignation.
Tension prevailed when the rally reached the Hubballi-Dharwad Municipal Corporation office.
Protesters allegedly attempted to burn portraits of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, and Mr. Kumar, triggering a scuffle between the police and the demonstrators.
The police, subsequently, detained several protesters.

Hubballi-Dharwad District Congress president Sadanand Danganavar, I.G. Sanadi, KPCC member Satish Meharwade, Shahzaman Mujahid, Anwar Mudgol, Mohammed Sharif Gargad, and several councillors and party functionaries participated in the protest.

article_sentences: India's opposition parties are set to march to the Supreme Court in Delhi to demand the resignation of the election chief over alleged voter fraud.
This will be the latest in a series of demonstrations in Delhi, with thousands of security forces deployed and roads barricaded in the capital.
Attempts to hold a protest by the Cockroach Janata Party pressure group over the weekend led to thousands of demonstrators being detained.
Opposition parties allege that under Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, India's voter rolls are being manipulated to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
Both the Election Commission and the BJP have rejected the charge.
The opposition lawmakers want to submit a memorandum to Chief Justice Surya Kant, but he has told reporters he declined the meeting citing "certain reasons".
He did not provide the reasons, but media reports citing the letter have said that he pointed out that some of the issues the opposition wanted to raise with him were also pending before the court.
The BBC has not seen the letter.
"Every Indian citizen has the right to approach the court, and we will hear their concerns and grant whatever is due under the law," he told reporters.
Congress MP Rahul Gandhi, meanwhile, has called "all opposition parties, civil society groups [and] all those who believe in democracy" to join Monday's march.

In a press conference on Monday, he shared a letter that he and Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge had written to the Chief Justice, laying out their concerns with Kumar's alleged conduct and with the contentious electoral roll revision.
He said that Kant had asked them to file a petition, which they would do at the end of their march.

article_sentences: The BJP on Monday (October 12, 2026) criticised the Congress over Rahul Gandhi’s request for a meeting with the Chief Justice of India (CJI), saying the judiciary must remain above day-to-day political battles.

In a post on X, BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia said, “From separation of powers to desperation for power, Rahul Gandhi has confused constitutional law with political theatre!” He said the CJI’s declining to meet Mr. Gandhi and Opposition leaders sent an important message: the judiciary must remain above day-to-day political battles.
Further attacking Mr. Gandhi, Mr. Bhatia said merely carrying a copy of the Constitution did not mean one understood it.
“Read it.
Respect it.
And learn the doctrine of separation of powers.
The Constitution is a guide to governance, not a prop for political performance!” he added.

Intensifying their agitation against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, the Opposition parties marched to the Supreme Court on Monday, with Mr. Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge seeking a meeting with Chief Justice Surya Kant to raise the issue of “vote chori.” The CJI, however, declined to meet Mr. Gandhi over the “vote chori” allegations, saying similar matters were sub judice in the Supreme Court, sources said.

Both Mr. Gandhi and Mr. Kharge had written to the CJI, seeking a meeting between 4 p.m. and 5 p.m. on Monday to hand over a memorandum, demanding an end to “vote chori,” the CEC’s resignation, the halting of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, and a switch back to the paper ballot format.

stories.summary: New Delhi , Oct 12 : Jantar Mantar has been de-notified as a designated venue for organising protests and demonstrations in Delhi, with the Delhi Police designating three new locations for the purpose, according to an official notice. The three new designated protest venues are Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi. The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) had constituted a committee to examine alternative venues for citizens to exercise their right to organise protests and demonstrations in place of the existing designated site. Based on the committee's recommendations, Jantar Mantar has been de-notified as a protest venue, the notice stated. Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar said that a detailed and revised Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for organising protests and demonstrations at the three designated venues would be issued separately. The notice partially modifies the earlier Standing Order dated April 28, 2022. The revised SOP is expected to lay down the procedures for organising protests and demonstrations at the newly designated venues. The development comes as leaders and parliamentarians of the opposition INDIA bloc launched a massive protest march from Connaught Place in central Delhi, intensifying their agitation against the Election Commission over alleged electoral manipulation and subversion of democratic institutions. Launching a fierce attack on the central government during the march, Congress General Secretary (Organisation) KC Venugopal described the Opposition's ongoing agitation as the "biggest andolan" against the poll panel and declared that the party is taking its legal battle to the apex court. "This is the biggest andolan against the Election Commissioner and the election system. Narendra Modi and Amit Shah are using the Chief Election Commissioner as their tool to destroy the democracy of this country, to hijack the democracy of the country," Venugopal said. Emphasizing that the Opposition will fight on both political and legal fronts, he said, "Therefore, for the last one week, we are on the streets. Today also we are going to be on the streets, and we are going to file a petition in the Supreme Court also." When asked by reporters regarding an appointment with the Chief Justice of India, Venugopal stated, "I don't want to comment on all that now. But anyway, we are going to fight legally also. We are going to the Supreme Court and file a petition there. The Supreme Court, Chief Justice informed us that between 10:00 to 4:00, they are ready to receive our petition; the registry is ready." Joining the protest, Congress MP Renuka Chowdhury condemned the police clampdown and accused the government of acting with impunity despite judicial safeguards. "This is a show of giving them assurance that we are going to fight for them, that we represent them and their voice should be heard here. This brute force here and declaring us unlawful is a clear show of violation of anything that is constitutional and disrespect to the Supreme Court which this government is showing," Chowdhury said. She added, "Despite the Supreme Court's rulings, they have violated and they have named us. You ask about SIR and they filed an FIR. One Gyanesh is more than 'Bharat desh'?" Former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee said, "We are demanding justice, nothing else. This is for people, for humankind, for justice...We want justice and nothing else." Against this backdrop, high security is in place in Central Delhi with barricades at multiple locations. Entry and exit at certain metro stations will also remain closed from 6:00 AM to 4:00 PM on October 12, 2026, for security reasons. The stations are Patel Chowk, Janpath, Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House, Central Secretariat, Barakhamba Road respectively. Security personnel have been deployed at Barakhamba Road, near Mandi House. article_sentences: For more than 75 years, the defining preoccupation of the Election Commission of India (ECI) has been “inclusion”.
The first general election of 1951-52 had to enrol an electorate of around 17 crore from scratch, many of whom were illiterate.
Successive Commissioners treated universal adult franchise as a promise to be fulfilled rather than just a principle to be stated on paper.
India could genuinely be proud of being an electoral democracy where voter turnout among the poor is higher than that among the rich, unlike in many western democracies.
The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls launched by the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) of India, Gyanesh Kumar, has reversed this progressive direction.

It was termed an exercise to “purify” the electoral rolls, but in practice, it is riddled with methodological flaws and ad hoc rule changes, resulting in the deletion of a large number of genuine voters.
The names of 13.37 crore people were struck off during the draft stage across 30 States and Union Territories in the three phases of the SIR.
The figure includes 65 lakh in Bihar, 6.57 crore in the 12 States and Union Territories covered in Phase 2, and 6.15 crore in Phase 3, whose final rolls are yet to be published.
The deletion rate doubled as SIR progressed — from 8.3% in Bihar to 12.9% in Phase 2 and 17% in Phase 3 (it was 32.8% in Delhi and 21.7% in Telangana).
In Phases 1 and 2, even after names were added back, net deletions were about 6.2 crore.
In Delhi, the draft roll has only 97.54 lakh electors, barely above the 94.95 lakh who voted in the February 2025 Assembly election.
In 24 of Delhi’s 70 constituencies, the draft roll now has fewer electors than the number who voted in the election.

stories.headline: Maharashtra Utility Opts For Thermal+Wind Power For RTC Supply, Cites Rising Data Centre Demand
stories.title: Maharashtra Utility Opts For Thermal+Wind Power For RTC Supply, Cites Rising Data Centre Demand
stories.summary: Nidar Utilities Panvel LLP (NUPLLP), a deemed distribution licensee serving the Panvel Special Economic Zone (SEZ), has secured regulatory approval for the procurement of 5 MW of round-the-clock (RTC) power through a combination of thermal and wind-based generation, citing rising electricity demand from data centres. The Maharashtra Electricity Regulatory Commission (MERC), in its latest order adopted tariffs of Rs 5.35/kWh for 2 MW of power from Manikaran Power Limited (MPL) and Rs 4.85/kWh for 3 MW from Arunachal Pradesh Power Corporation Private Limited (APPCPL). The Commission also approved the associated power purchase agreements (PPAs) under Section 63 of the Electricity Act, 2003. The 2 MW procurement from MPL covers the period from February 1, 2026, to January 31, 2027, while the 3 MW supply from APPCPL is scheduled for April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2027. Both tariffs are applicable at the Maharashtra State Transmission Utility (STU) periphery. Additional Power Requirement According to the petition, NUPLLP's total load is around 18 MW. Its existing power portfolio includes 3 MW of small hydro power, 5 MW contracted with MPL, 7 MW contracted with PTC India, and approximately 3.5 MW procured through power exchanges. The additional short-term procurement is intended to strengthen its contracted supply and meet consumer demand. The growing electricity requirements of data centres are a key factor behind the procurement. NUPLLP stated that its data centre consumers had sought an increase in contract demand from 20,000 kVA to 28,000 kVA. The additional requirement is expected to materialise in phases, prompting the licensee to arrange power accordingly to avoid being left with stranded capacity. Data centres account for approximately 95% of the consumer mix, according to the petition. For the second procurement requirement, NUPLLP initially invited bids for 5 MW of RTC power for the period from April 1, 2026, to March 31, 2027. Following a request from a prospective bidder, it reduced the minimum bid quantity from 5 MW to 2 MW to encourage participation. APPCPL was ultimately selected for 3 MW of supply, with Apraava Renewable Energy Private Limited identified as the generation source. The first procurement involved 2 MW from MPL, with Birla Carbon India Private Limited's Patalganga unit in Maharashtra identified as the source. MERC's order identifies the source for the APPCPL procurement as Apraava Renewable Energy Private Limited, with wind generation specified in the Commission's tariff-comparison discussion. Both procurement requirements received only one bid each. The bidders did not lower their initial price offers during the electronic reverse auction conducted on January 2, 2026. NUPLLP subsequently sought regulatory approval for the discovered tariffs and the PPAs executed with the two suppliers. Reasonable Tariffs: MERC MERC found the tariffs reasonable and comparable with prevailing short-term power prices. The Commission noted that tariffs discovered for short-term RTC power on the DEEP portal ranged from Rs 4.62/kWh to Rs 10/kWh. It concluded that the rates of Rs 5.35/kWh and Rs 4.85/kWh met the requirements for tariff adoption under Section 63 of the Electricity Act, 2003. The petition also highlighted the additional costs associated with procuring power through exchanges. NUPLLP stated that inter-state transmission charges and losses could add approximately Rs 0.65–0.80/kWh when electricity is delivered from the Central Transmission Utility (CTU) regional periphery to Maharashtra's STU periphery. It also pointed to the risk of power not being cleared in certain time blocks during periods of high demand, potentially exposing the licensee to deviation settlement mechanism (DSM) penalties. MERC has also clarified that NUPLLP may procure additional power if demand exceeds its contracted capacity. The licensee can undertake fresh short-term competitive bidding or procure electricity through power exchanges, subject to the applicable Multi-Year Tariff (MYT) Regulations and other legal requirements. The order reinforces the importance of securing dependable power supplies as data-centre electricity demand rises, while allowing NUPLLP to add capacity in phases in line with its consumers' requirements.

stories.title: "Environmental Protection Not Just Govt's Job, Citizens Equally Responsible": CM Omar
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 12 : Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Monday said environmental protection cannot be the government's responsibility alone and called for collective public participation, even as he cautioned against any abrupt curbs on tourism that sustains thousands of families in the region. Speaking at the J&K Agriculture Science Congress 2026 at Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir (SKUAST-K), CM Omar Abdullah said the Union Territory was already facing the consequences of climate change, marked by erratic snowfall, water scarcity, landslides and floods. He said snowfall has become increasingly irregular, with insufficient winter precipitation hitting water availability in the following months. People face shortages in March, April and May, he said, only to see heavy rain and rising river levels later, triggering flood and landslide risks. This is our new reality. This is the reality we are living with," CM Omar said, stressing the need to sustain livelihoods while pursuing development. The Chief Minister said climate change cannot be fought by any single region or country in isolation and demands coordinated global action, while local communities must own the responsibility of protecting their surroundings and natural resources. On tourism, CM Omar said its environmental footprint must be addressed without disregarding the livelihoods of those dependent on the sector. He warned against suddenly restricting tourist arrivals, noting that tourism is the mainstay of many local families and businesses, and said any regulation of visitor numbers would have to be gradual and balanced. While conceding that tourism exerts pressure on the environment, he said tourists and vehicles alone cannot be blamed for pollution, plastic waste and water scarcity. He asked whether areas with negligible tourist activity were free of garbage and plastic pollution, and urged residents to look inward at their own practices. CM Omar came down heavily on the habit of throwing waste from vehicles and public transport, saying citizens must stop littering and take greater ownership of keeping their surroundings clean. He also urged people to cut down on single-use plastic bags by carrying reusable bags while shopping. Underlining the need for resource conservation, he asked people to avoid wasting water and to switch off lights, fans and heaters when not in use. The Chief Minister said that while the government has the primary responsibility for environmental protection, real change will come only through active public participation, and that sustainability and conservation can be achieved only when official action is matched by responsible citizen behaviour. (KNS).

stories.title: Haryana Govt Issues 100 MWp Rooftop Solar Tender With Seven-Yrs Maintenance
stories.summary: Haryana government has issued a tender for the tentative development of 100 MWp of grid-connected rooftop (GCRT) solar plants without battery banks. The bidder design, supply, erect, test and commission rooftop solar projects. The developer will also be required to provide comprehensive maintenance for seven years at various locations across Haryana and Chandigarh. It has sought bids till October 30, 2026 The scope of the rooftop solar project includes the supply of solar generation meters and bidirectional meters. The goods supplied under the contract must be fully insured by the supplier, at its own cost, against any loss or damage arising during manufacture or acquisition, transportation and delivery to the site. Once the materials have been delivered to the user site, the user department or organisation may provide a storage facility, with a lock-and-key arrangement for the supplier, for a maximum of 15 days. This provision is based on the assumption that the systems will be installed within 15 days of delivery. Generating Solar Power, Adding Meter & Bidirectional Meter The bidder is expected to add solar generation meter and bidirectional meter, along with current transformers (CTs) and potential transformers (PTs), where required and add a surge protection device (SPD). The developer also must comply with the latest specifications and accuracy classes prescribed under the applicable Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission ( HERC ) and DISCOM instructions at the time of installation. The bidder must supply components such as wires, cables, switches, circuit breakers, connectors, junction boxes, changeover switches and other associated components the scope of the work. It would aleo be required to meet the latest applicable International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) and Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) standards. Scope of Work The size and weight of the packing cases must take into consideration, where appropriate, the remoteness of the goods' final destination and the absence of heavy handling facilities at any point during transit. The scope of work also includes performance testing of the complete project, after-sales service through service centres, and coverage of the risk liability of all personnel associated with the project's implementation and execution. Following commissioning, the successful bidder must train at least one person nominated by the user at each location on various aspects of the project's design and maintenance. The successful bidder must maintain sufficient inventories of spare parts to ensure that the project remains functional throughout the warranty period. The bidder must also operate the project on a trial basis and closely monitor its performance before handing it over.

stories.headline: Manipur: 7 banned groups call shutdown on October 15 over 1949 merger with India
stories.title: Manipur: 7 banned groups call shutdown on October 15 over 1949 merger with India
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The shutdown call comes amid fresh Kuki-Naga clashes that killed nine people in Manipur’s hill districts.

Imphal: Seven banned insurgent groups in Manipur have called for a statewide shutdown on October 15 to mark what they describe as “National Black Day”, protesting the state’s merger with the Indian Union in 1949.

The shutdown call comes amid renewed violence in Manipur’s hill districts, where nine people were killed in a fresh round of clashes involving members of the Kuki and Naga communities on Friday and Saturday.
The Coordination Committee (CorCom), an umbrella organisation comprising six banned underground outfits, has announced a 12-hour shutdown from 6 am to 6 pm on October 15.

The groups are the Kangleipak Communist Party (KCP), Kanglei Yawol Kanna Lup (KYKL), People’s Revolutionary Party of Kangleipak (PREPAK), PREPAK-Pro, Revolutionary People’s Front (RPF) and United National Liberation Front (UNLF).
The Socialist Revolutionary Party (SOREPA), which is not part of the six-member coalition, has separately called for a 12-hour shutdown from 5 am to 5 pm on the same day.
Both organisations have said essential services, including medical emergencies, media operations and religious activities, will be exempted.
Why are the groups protesting?
In separate statements, CorCom and SOREPA said October 15 is observed annually to protest Manipur’s merger with India.
Referring to the state by its former name, Kangleipak, the outfits alleged that the merger violated international and domestic legal provisions.

They cited Article 2(4) of the United Nations Charter, the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties, the Manipur State Constitution Act, 1947, and the Indian Independence Act, 1947, in support of their claims.

The groups also alleged that the then ruler, King Bodhchandra, was pressured into signing the Manipur Merger Agreement in Shillong on September 21, 1949, claiming he was under house arrest and at gunpoint.
